title: Vendor-agnostic automated PACE/multi-path transport orchestration and single-pane tactical NetOps for S6/G6 at brigade and below (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF)

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: the Army's own UNO page states the goal is to 'simplify and reduce the number of network management tools' S6s/G6s use (https://peoc3t.army.mil/i2s/uno.php, 2024-2025); FACT/MEDIUM: PC-C6 (July 2026) still logged 'semi-frequent connectivity drops' at division scale (DefenseScoop 2026-07-31). Stalled fires/COP traffic during jamming or movement is operationally serious, though not the single limiting factor for the formation.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: every movement, terrain change or jamming event on a 3-5 transport network forces a manual PACE decision; the pain recurs in every exercise cited (Ivy Sting, Lightning Surge 2026-04, PC-C6 2026-07) and in daily garrison-to-field transitions. Not 5 because the sharpest failures cluster around contested/EW conditions rather than continuously.

FACT/MEDIUM: money exists in the NGC2 C2 Transport sub-line (~$1.36B FY26 request; DefenseScoop 2025-07-02) but it is integrated by team leads (Anduril, Lockheed), not disbursed to a neutral adapter vendor; UNO/INB2 licensing amounts are not public; FY26 NDAA 50% obligation cap and HASC FY27 $710M proposed cut (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20) constrain the line. No identifiable budget line buys 'vendor-agnostic orchestration' as such. Requests are not obligations.

Score of 1 explained: every slot is held by an incumbent under a live action - CodeMettle INB2 with a May-2025 sole-source-style license/PDSS notice (fbodaily 2025-05-30, FACT/MEDIUM), UNO prototype OTAs to RII/CodeMettle and QinetiQ US via C5 consortium (ASDNews 2024-12-30), NGC2 OTAs to Team Anduril and Team Lockheed (army.mil 287180, 2025-07) with the Army preferring team-lead integration. The UNO MA IDIQ cannot be confirmed as awarded (Public evidence insufficient). Only entry is as a sub-tier component supplier to one of these primes; no open competition a new entrant could win is evidenced.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: policy-based multi-path failover over commercial transports is a solved SD-WAN-class problem and a container agent with SNMP/REST adapters is buildable; but the hard part - normalising MANET vendor telemetry and moving flows without vendor northbound APIs - is unproven (DARPA MINC with Peraton/BAE has no public transition; DIU ORIENT awardees remain prototype-stage per public evidence).

HYPOTHESIS (card estimates, unsourced): $150k-$350k buys a commercial-hardware proof of concept, but a credible military demo is estimated at $1.5M-$3M because it needs PoR-class radios, cleared U.S.-person engineers and exercise participation. $250k covers only the PoC, which the card itself says produces 'a demo the buyer cannot use'.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: a commercial-transport field demo (Doodle Labs/Starlink/5G CPE/HF ALE) is achievable in 3-6 months, but a demo the Army recognises requires PoR radio adapters (ITAR/NDA-gated), a NetModX or exercise slot and prime sponsorship - 12-18 months minimum and gated on vendor cooperation that is not evidenced.

FACT/MEDIUM: commercial radio, Starlink and 5G CPE telemetry are obtainable by purchase and public docs; but PoR radio management-interface docs (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris) require NDAs, U.S.-person handling and often ITAR authorisation, and real jamming traces, spectrum and PACE plans are CUI/classified and not obtainable pre-award (card data_requirement; E07).

Score of 1 explained: the product sits on ITAR technical data (radio management planes), CUI (network/spectrum plans), RMF/ATO on DODIN-A, potential NSA CSfC review and SIPR-level integration needing facility and personnel clearances (card regulatory_burden 'high'). Per E07 (FACT/HIGH): 22 CFR 120.62/126.18 give no deemed-export exception for a domestic foreign-person employee, so the Indonesian founder would need a DSP-5 license to receive PoR radio data; 32 CFR 117 FOCI treats any non-citizen as a foreign interest; SBIR requires >50% U.S.-citizen/LPR ownership (13 CFR 121.702). These are constraints requiring export, immigration and government-contracts counsel, not legal conclusions - but they are unusually dense for this gap.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the MVP is fully unclassified on commercial hardware with synthetic traces, and the DDIL emulation variant stays unclassified indefinitely; but the card rates classification dependence 'eventually' - the first PoR integration and any TNO/UNO SIPR work bring CUI, ITAR and clearance needs all at once.

Score of 1 explained (5 = least intense): eleven named competitor groups occupy every layer - CodeMettle (INB2, fielded), RII and QinetiQ US (UNO OTAs), Anduril+Klas and Lockheed (NGC2 full stacks), Persistent (Cloud Relay; NGC2 network selection 2025-10), Silvus/Motorola (closed 2025-08, SEC 8-K), L3Harris/GDMS (PoR radios), PM Tactical Network's Seeker Auto-PACE, Peraton/BAE (MINC), Aalyria/Viasat/Higher Ground/IoT-AI (ORIENT), REDCOM. Most are well capitalised and hold the interfaces.

FACT/MEDIUM: incumbents have visible weaknesses - tool sprawl persists despite INB2, PC-C6 still had connectivity drops, Seeker does not reach MANET management planes, and each vendor fix re-creates single-vendor lock-in - but they own the contracts and APIs and can each add automation under existing OTAs ('None needs a startup's help', card incumbent_response). Vulnerability is real for the buyer, not exploitable by an outsider.

Score of 1 explained: the card's who_controls_the_interface states a startup controls none of the required interfaces - radio/terminal vendors control device APIs, CPE C2IN and NGC2 team leads control NGC2 APIs (schemas 'still being co-defined'), PdM TCNO and its primes control TNO/INB2 points, NSA/CSfC governs the encrypted path. No PoR radio vendor is evidenced to expose a licensable northbound API to third parties, and vendors have commercial incentive not to (Persistent expanding closed Cloud Relay to Azure, 2025-09/10).

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: path-selection algorithms are well known (MINC, SD-WAN); the only durable assets would be an adapter library and an accreditation footprint, both of which depend on access the vendors control and which incumbents could replicate under their existing contracts (card defensibility: 'weak against vendors who own the interfaces').

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: multi-transport failover and single-pane monitoring have commercial analogues (public safety FirstNet+LMR+SATCOM, mining/energy mesh+LTE+SATCOM, maritime, disaster response), but commercial SD-WAN already covers the wired/cellular/SATCOM case and the differentiating military features (MANET adapters, PACE-as-code, EW awareness) have a thin commercial market (card dual_use 'medium').

FACT/MEDIUM: second buyers voice the same need (USSOCOM TACLAN/SDN 'King for a Day' RFI 2026-05-15; ACC AMIC Deployable Tactical Communications RFI, responses due 2026-02-25) and allied land forces (D-LBO, LE TacCIS) are re-buying multi-transport networks, so a working product could expand into spectrum/cyber awareness and other services - but these are RFIs, not awards, and the allied integration slot is also incumbent-held (Rheinmetall/blackned, Systematic, Thales).

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: NetOps software is bought as enterprise licenses plus PDSS/sustainment (INB2 May-2025 action shows the recurring-license model) and per-division-set deployment would recur across NGC2 fielding; but the amounts are not public and the recurring stream accrues to whoever holds the license, currently CodeMettle.

Score of 1 explained: three of five required roles the card marks fatal_if_absent (recent Army signal officer/255N, tactical RF/MANET engineer, cleared U.S.-person ITAR-handling engineer) are absent; the Indonesian founder cannot lawfully receive the PoR radio technical data the adapter layer needs without a DSP-5 (22 CFR 120.62/126.18, E07 FACT/HIGH) and cannot hold a clearance; the German founder is clearance-eligible only after naturalisation (~2031-2032 at earliest, INFERENCE); SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership must be engineered on the cap table; and ~$250k is roughly one-tenth of the estimated cost of a credible military demo. The German founder's route into the Bundeswehr D-LBO/blackned ecosystem is the one genuine fit, but that is an allied market, not the founders' stated primary U.S. target.

market.summary: No distinct budget owner for vendor-agnostic PACE orchestration; NGC2 transport money is integrated by primes (Anduril/Klas, Lockheed), UNO/INB2 amounts are not public and Congress has capped/cut the NGC2 line; demand signal is RFI/exercise-shaped, not purchase-order-shaped (2022 requirement still unfielded cross-vendor in 2026); addressable spend for a neutral adapter vendor is plausibly tens of millions over several years versus $1.5M-$3M demo and $8M-$15M deployment cost estimates. Weighed: ACCEPTED - the card and my own read find no budget line or vehicle that pays a neutral third party.

competition.summary: Both halves are already government-assigned: CodeMettle INB2 (fielded, sole-source-style 2025 action) owns single-pane NetOps; PM Tactical Network runs Seeker Auto-PACE; Anduril and Lockheed hold NGC2 full-stack OTAs (transport through application) and Anduril's Klas acquisition closed the edge-box seam; radio vendors (Silvus/Motorola, Persistent, L3Harris) own the telemetry APIs with no incentive to open them; MINC and ORIENT stalled in prototype purgatory; UNO MA IDIQ unconfirmed. Weighed: ACCEPTED - the strongest of the three; the incumbent_response section of the card reaches the same 'mostly REJECT' conclusion.

feasibility.summary: ITAR (22 CFR 120.62/126.18) blocks the non-U.S.-person founder from PoR radio management data without a DSP-5; FOCI and clearance rules exclude both founders from SIPR-level integration for years; SBIR ownership test requires cap-table restructuring; capital covers ~10% of a credible military demo; the commercial-hardware MVP 'produces a demo the buyer cannot use'. Weighed: ACCEPTED - cross-checked against evidence/E07.json, which supports each regulatory claim at FACT/HIGH; these are constraints for counsel, not legal conclusions, but they are dispositive for sequencing.

verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute with strength 4-5 and I find no evidence that rebuts them; the card's own incumbent_response ('Mostly REJECT as a standalone company') and killer_risk sections agree. Applying the chain test: PROBLEM (documented, FACT/HIGH) -> USER (S6/G6 NetOps cells, FACT) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER (Army CIO/G-6 Unified Network Plan 2.0, C2 CFT; INFERENCE) -> PROGRAM OFFICE (PdM TCNO / PM Tactical Network inside CPE C2IN; FACT, post-reorg names unverified) -> CONTRACTING OFFICE (ACC-APG, C5 consortium/CMG; INFERENCE) -> BUDGET (NGC2 transport sub-line and UNO/INB2 O&M; exists but prime-channelled and congressionally constrained) -> CONTRACT VEHICLE: BREAK. Every vehicle at the end of the chain (INB2 sole-source-style license, UNO OTAs to RII/QinetiQ, NGC2 OTAs to Anduril/Lockheed) is held by an incumbent, and the UNO MA IDIQ that would open competition cannot be confirmed awarded (Public evidence insufficient). The major penalty applies. Two independent, individually sufficient kill reasons remain: (1) market/structural - the buyer procures prime-led, vertically integrated stacks and radio vendors own the northbound interfaces, so a neutral orchestration layer has no buyer and no interface access, as four to five years of MINC/ORIENT/UNO prototype purgatory demonstrate; (2) team-specific - the one asset that would make the product usable by the Army (cross-PoR-vendor adapters) requires ITAR technical data the Indonesian founder cannot lawfully receive and clearances neither founder can hold, while $250k funds only a commercial-radio demo the card itself calls 'a demo the buyer cannot use'. Confidence in the kill is HIGH on direction even though several individual facts (Seeker article date, Persistent $87.5M award, UNO IDIQ status) are MEDIUM/LOW and not re-verified this session; none of them would flip the verdict if corrected. The narrower variants the skeptics offer (DDIL emulation harness; commercial-only SD-WAN for public safety/mining) are not G10 surviving - they address a different pain (test/training tooling; non-defense connectivity) and should be evaluated as separate candidates, not carried forward under this gap.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline - killed. For completeness, the only adjacent variant all three skeptics agree is survivable is NOT the orchestrator: a DDIL network-emulation / hardware-in-the-loop test harness (synthetic and recorded link traces, commercial mesh/Starlink/5G CPE hardware, no ITAR radio data, no crypto path) aimed at the Army SBIR 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' topic (armysbir.army.mil, 2025) and sold to UNO/NGC2 primes as a test tool. It is legally accessible to both founders today but is a smaller, services-adjacent tooling market with the same SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership constraint (13 CFR 121.702), and it should be scored as its own gap rather than as G10. A second adjacent path - the German founder entering the Bundeswehr D-LBO/blackned/Rheinmetall ecosystem where commercial radios are not ITAR-gated - improves interface access but not market size and contradicts the founders' primary U.S. focus.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, the only thing they could legally and affordably build first is a container-based transport-telemetry and PACE-as-code agent on commercial hardware: Doodle Labs or Rajant mesh, a Starlink terminal, a private-5G CPE on Open5GS, an HF ALE modem, a per-flow policy engine, a DDIL-tolerant local time-series store and a browser HMI that auto-generates the S6's network status slide, with a published open telemetry schema and adapter SDK (roughly $150k-$350k, HYPOTHESIS). They would show it to a division G6 of an NGC2 unit (4ID, 25ID, III Corps, I Corps) and to PdM TCNO through a NetModX or xTech entry, and the 8-10 node field test with induced degradation would prove sub-second detection and automated flow migration versus manual PACE on time-to-recover and packet loss. The customer would care because PC-C6 still produced semi-frequent connectivity drops (DefenseScoop 2026-07-31) and the Army's own UNO goal is fewer tools and less signal-soldier workload. But this is exactly where it fails: the demo runs on radios the Army does not field at scale, and the step that would make it usable - adapters for Silvus, Persistent and L3Harris PoR radios - requires ITAR technical data and vendor NDAs that the Indonesian founder cannot receive without a DSP-5 and that the vendors have no incentive to grant, while Anduril (owning Lattice Mesh and the Klas edge box under an NGC2 full-stack OTA), Lockheed, CodeMettle/RII under existing UNO OTAs, and PM Tactical Network's Seeker can each add a policy layer inside contracts they already hold. An incumbent does not need to crush them; it only needs to keep the interface closed. The milestone that would justify the next $2-5M - a signed, licensable northbound API agreement with at least one PoR radio vendor plus a subcontract letter from a UNO or NGC2 prime for a specific component, with a U.S.-person-controlled cap table and a cleared engineer in place - is precisely the milestone this team, as constituted and capitalised, has no evidenced path to reach, which is why the gap is killed rather than deferred.
bear_case_summary: The problem is real but every slot is taken and gated: CodeMettle INB2 holds fielded battalion-and-below NetOps under a 2025 sole-source-style action; UNO prototypes belong to RII/CodeMettle and QinetiQ US; PM Tactical Network already runs Seeker Auto-PACE at the hub layer; Anduril (with Klas) and Lockheed own NGC2 transport-through-application stacks and the Army wants team leads to integrate; Silvus/Motorola, Persistent and L3Harris own the northbound APIs and are consolidating rather than opening them. Better-funded neutral attempts (DARPA MINC, DIU ORIENT) have not transitioned in 4-5 years. Budget exists only as prime-channelled NGC2 money that Congress has capped and proposed cutting, and no line buys a neutral orchestrator. For this team specifically, the adapter layer needs ITAR-controlled radio data the Indonesian founder cannot lawfully receive, clearances neither founder can hold for years, an SBIR cap table that must be restructured, and $1.5M-$3M for a demo the Army would recognise against $250k in hand.
bull_case_summary: The pain is documented by the Army itself (UNO's stated goal of fewer tools; PC-C6 connectivity drops; a 'multi-path transport-agnostic' requirement standing since December 2022), multi-transport networks (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF) now exist at scale for the first time, NGC2 nominally requires 'government-approved non-proprietary APIs' at the transport layer, second buyers (USSOCOM TACLAN/SDN, ACC AMIC) are asking the same question in 2026 RFIs, and allied forces re-buying tactical networks are less locked to U.S. radio vendors. A neutral, open adapter and PACE-as-code layer is something no incumbent wants to build because it commoditises their controllers. If CPE C2IN enforced the non-proprietary-API rule as a separately procured line, or a PoR radio vendor published a licensable northbound API, or the UNO MA IDIQ opened with room for new entrants, the technical wedge would become a fundable component business - but none of these is evidenced today, and none is within this team's control.
